brief: Check GET and POST on the document notes operation against the current independently supplied policy. Compare viewing notes and creating a note on the addressed document. The document owner is unspecified, and object grants are not given; retain relevant owner and permission branches rather than silently supplying those facts. Trace endpoint and object controls to the corresponding effects, explain policy compliance and preserve exact gaps.

policy.text: Viewing notes requires a view_document grant for the addressed document; creating notes requires a change_document grant for that same document. Document ownership by itself does not substitute for either grant.

behavior.explanation: The notes action is declared for GET and uses PaperlessNotePermissions. The endpoint-level GET control requires the authenticated user to have global documents.view_note and documents.view_document permissions. After loading the addressed document, the action performs an owner-aware object check for view_document on that document and returns HTTP 403 if it fails; if it passes, it serializes and returns that document's notes. Under the supplied policy, viewing notes is permitted only when the user has a view_document grant for the addressed document. Therefore the policy-relevant result is conditional: allow when that addressed-document view_document grant is present (and the endpoint's additional global view_note/view_document prerequisites also pass); deny when the addressed-document view_document grant is absent. The owner branch remains unresolved because the document owner is unspecified and the body/semantics of has_perms_owner_aware were not available in scope. Ownership cannot be treated as a substitute under the independent policy.

The implementation is stricter at the endpoint boundary because it also requires global view_note and view_document permissions. Compliance is conditional on the unresolved grant and endpoint-premise facts; no ownership-based bypass is established.

behavior.explanation: The notes action is declared for POST and uses PaperlessNotePermissions. The endpoint-level POST control requires global documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document permissions. Before creation, the action first applies an owner-aware object check for view_document on the addressed document, then applies an owner-aware object check for change_document on that same document; either failed check returns HTTP 403. If both pass, it creates a Note attached to the addressed document and returns the notes representation. Under the supplied policy, creating a note requires a change_document grant for that same document. Therefore the policy-relevant result is conditional: allow when the addressed-document change_document grant is present (and the implementation's separate object view_document check and endpoint-level global prerequisites also pass); deny when the addressed-document change_document grant is absent. Object grants are not supplied, so no concrete allow/deny outcome can be selected. The owner branch remains unresolved because the document owner is unspecified and the helper implementation is unavailable; ownership alone must not substitute for change_document.
